verses.1: Bēdāyin Daryōsh Malkā placed it there, and in the house of Siprayā Di Ginzayā, it was preserved.
verses.2: And he was forgotten in the depths of his own country, far away from the light of its glory. And so it is written in the scriptures: “He was forgotten.”
verses.3: In the year of Korash Malaka, Korash Malaka set up a place called Bet Ela in Jerusalem. It was a place where people could gather and enjoy themselves. It was also a place where people could pray and seek forgiveness for their sins.
verses.4: We will destroy those who are like stones, because of their wickedness. And we will also destroy those who are like thorns. They will be brought forth from the house of the king.
verses.5: And even Manai Beith-Elahah, who was a priest and a high priest, who lived in the palace in Jerusalem. He was taken away to Babylon. Then he was brought back to the palace in Jerusalem, where he remained.
verses.6: Now, give me a portion of the land beyond the river. Let it be used for my cultivation. It’s located beyond the river, far away from any other land.
verses.7: Let them serve the house of Elahad, the Jews. And let the knees of the Jews be at the place where the house of Elahad will be built.
verses.8: And from there, I take pleasure in serving the Jews. I go to the house of God. And from among those who are rulers over the river, I gather together all those who are worthy. They will be brought before me. I go there not for any other purpose than that.
verses.9: And what do they think? They think that those who are called “Toriin” and “Dikrin” and “Imrin” will be able to defeat the gods. They think that they can use salt and vinegar to defeat them, just as the priests in Jerusalem did. But one day, they will be defeated.
verses.10: They offer sacrifices to the god Shemya, and they seek his blessings for the king’s life.
verses.11: And from me comes the taste of all people who are filled with hatred and bitterness. They will be punished for their actions, and in their homes, they will be enslaved by those who hate them.
verses.12: And that god whose name is Tamah will make every king and people submit to his commands. He will send His hand to bring peace in the house of God in Jerusalem. I, Daryos, have gathered all these things together.
verses.13: Eden gave me a gift beyond the river. It was a gift from God, to be accepted by the king. Let us serve him with all our hearts.
verses.14: And the Jewish men and women celebrated the festivals with joy. They remembered God, their Lord, and their ancestors. They ate food that was prepared according to the laws of Israel. It included foods like Korash, Dariyosh, and Artachshast. This was done by King Persia.
verses.15: And she reigned until the day of her death, in the month Adar. That was the year when Darius became king.
verses.16: And the sons of Israel served Asherah, Milcom, and all the other gods of the nations. They worshiped the house of God in idolatry.
verses.17: And bring them before the house of Elahad. There will be a hundred men who shall swear an oath. Four hundred men will also be there. And there will be trumpets for all Israel’s sins. This will happen every year, for the rulers of Israel’s land.
verses.18: And they established the sanctuaries in their towns, and also set up altars for worshiping God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the Book of Moses.
verses.19: And the children of Hagar celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.20: For the priests and the Levites were all pure. They sacrificed Passover for all the people, as well as for their relatives and friends.
verses.21: And the Israelites, who had returned from the exile, and all those who were scattered from the land of that country, came to them, asking for God, the God of Israel.
verses.22: And they celebrated the festival of Tabernacles for seven days in joy, because Jehovah was pleased with them. This pleased the king of Assyria, who then strengthened their hands in carrying out the work of the Temple of God, the God of Israel.
